label: Regular car
description: Compact and mid-size cars. Electronics 0.22 kW in total: control units, pumps, lights, steering and brakes 0.15 + screens and audio 0.05 + camera/radar driver assistance 0.02. Cabin: walls and windows 45 W/K; fresh air 100 m³/h when heating (against fogged windows) and 45 m³/h when cooling (mostly recirculated air); 1.0 m² effective sun area (glass area × transmittance × angle); 200 kJ/K heat capacity (air, seats, dashboard)
source: Electronics: Argonne measured 144–226 W of non-climate load in two EVs at 22 °C (DOE Vehicle Technologies Office, Program Record 'Impact of Cold Ambient Temperature and Extreme Conditions on EVs', Sep 2024, Table 2); Zhang & He 2026 (arXiv 2605.05919) use 250 W. Driver assistance: camera/radar systems draw tens of watts. Cabin: chosen so that the heat balance reproduces the stationary measurements in measurements.csv (Argonne, ADAC) within about ±30 %; heat capacity from the Tesla Model 3 cold-start energy (≈200 kJ/K, Zhang & He 2026 from TEEL dynamometer data)

label: Large or premium car
description: Large or premium cars with large screens and a driver-assistance computer. Electronics 0.42 kW in total: 0.20 + screens and audio 0.10 + assistance computer and sensors 0.12. Cabin: same walls and fresh air as a regular car (the measurements show no larger heating need for large cars); 1.2 m² effective sun area (larger glass, glass roof); 230 kJ/K; stronger blower
source: Assistance computer: Tesla's HW3 computer draws under 100 W (Tesla Autonomy Day 2019, reported by Electrek); NVIDIA DRIVE Orin modules up to 60 W each; Gawron et al. 2018 (Environ. Sci. Technol. 52:3249) assume about 200 W for a Level-4 computer. Production assistance computers therefore draw about 0.05–0.2 kW, far below the Facts tab's 0.8–2.5 kW. Cabin: ADAC 2024 summer traffic-jam test, Tesla Model Y at 35 °C with sun lamps: 1.5 kW in total (measurements.csv)
